checklist: cert/import.mjs: import cryptography 50.0.2 from /node_modules/@ai-ecoverse/py-cryptography, found by discovery without PYTHONPATH, no nested python, importlib.metadata names 50.0.2; its side module cryptography.hazmat.bindings._rust imports (with _openssl inside, which imports py-cffi's _cffi_backend)

cert/primitives.mjs: backend.openssl_version_text() is the bundled 'OpenSSL 3.5.9 …'; SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA3-256, BLAKE2b, HMAC-SHA256 and PBKDF2 give the known answers; AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-CBC and Fernet round-trip; the error paths raise Python exceptions, not a panic=abort trap: a bad HMAC InvalidSignature, a flipped AES-GCM tag InvalidTag, a Fernet token under another key InvalidToken, a broken PEM key ValueError; the cffi Binding pyOpenSSL uses calls OpenSSL_version(_num)

cert/keys.mjs: azure/cli/core/keys.py's generate_ssh_keys as az vm create --generate-ssh-keys runs it (RSA 2048, PEM TraditionalOpenSSL private key written 0600, OpenSSH ssh-rsa public key) and its reload of the existing private key; RS256 (msal's client assertion), PSS and OAEP; an encrypted PKCS8 key refuses a wrong password with ValueError; P-256 ECDSA with an ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 OpenSSH key, P-384 ECDH, Ed25519 with an OpenSSH private key round trip, X25519; every wrong signature raises InvalidSignature

cert/x509.mjs: a P-256 CA signs the leaf of an RSA CSR (SAN, EKU clientAuth, AKI); the key+certificate PEM az's certificate service-principal login reads loads (key and certificate match), the leaf verifies against its CA, its SHA-1 thumbprint is the SHA-1 of its DER (what auth/identity.py takes through pyOpenSSL), DER and PKCS12 with the CA chain round-trip, a broken certificate raises ValueError

cert/threads.mjs: 4 Python threads hash (equal to hashlib) and sign/verify with Ed25519 at once, so the side module's thread-local state works on each kernel thread; python.wasm's ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION and _rust's openssl_version_text() are the same OpenSSL 3.5.9, and ssl.create_default_context() still works with both copies loaded

cert/notices.mjs: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md names OpenSSL (Apache-2.0), cffi (MIT-0, its headers are in the generated _openssl.c) and the wasix-org Rust standard library, each with its licence text, and (scripts/rust-crate-notices.mjs, checked against cargo tree by check-rust-notices.mjs at build) every crate _rust links

build.sh (scripts/rust-pyext/check-side-module.mjs): _rust has dylink.0, exports PyModExport__rust and the TLS entry points, every env/GOT import is exported by wasix-python 3.15.0-8's python.wasm, no import of an OpenSSL name (its own copy binds to itself, -Bsymbolic), and wasm-opt --metrics counts no Try/TryTable/Throw/ThrowRef/Rethrow (python.wasm is legacy EH)
